newsitem.title: CANADA: UGG CEO challenges Pools to extend bid.
newsitem.headline: UGG CEO challenges Pools to extend bid.

text.p: Bidders in a C$172 million hostile takeover of United Grain Growers Ltd should extend their offer to 60 days to avoid triggering a poison pill if they believe theirs is the only bid, UGG's chief executive officer said on Monday.

"If there's no rival bid, then they should be very comfortable making a permitted bid, one that's for all the shares and it's open for 60 days," UGG chief executive Brian Hayward told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Alberta Wheat Pool and Manitoba Pool Elevators made a C$13.75 a share offer to buy all UGG limited common voting shares February 20. The offer expires March 27, 35 days later.
UGG shares fell C$0.20 at 1300 EST to C$14.20 on the Toronto Stock Exchange Monday as 12,519 shares changed hands.
UGG's directors on February 14 adopted a plan for a massive dilution of shares in case any one shareholder bought more than 15 percent of its stock.
The pools said they had bought up to 14.98 percent February 13 and had a deal to buy 6.4 percent more.
UGG said the poison pill, which includes a 60-day cooling off period, had been triggered by this. The pools said it was not.
Any such massive dilution was believed to be an unprecidented event in Canada.

"We would rather (get an opinion on the poison pill) later than sooner so we could clearly show there's no competing bid and that our value is thw highest value, we're quite confident about that, "Griffiths McBurney & Partners managing partner of corporate finance Thomas Budd said earlier monday.
